claim: The ledger's bias points toward STOP BUILDING. The defect can only move a counter from STOP to STOP BUILDING, never the reverse.
evidence: The claim is right about the defect itself. offerAppeared(...) at UnlockOfferLedger.swift:223-226 only demotes offerAppeared to offerUnavailable, and STOP needs offerAppeared > 0 (PLAN-STAGE1.md:531-533). But the heading and summary describe the ledger's overall bias, and the code also has a path that pushes the other way. RoadView.swift:57 puts `.onAppear { model.recordOfferAppeared() }` on the whole ScrollView (RoadView.swift:51-57). The offer card comes after `header`, `tokaido` and `west` (RoadView.swift:40-43), which together hold all 16 stretch rows (RoadView.swift:75-77, 99-101; 'sixteen-stretch' at :14). So `offerAppeared` is recorded as soon as the screen opens with the product loaded, even if the price is below the fold and the rider never scrolls to it. §K's STOP text says "the offer itself rendered with a price in front of them" (PLAN-STAGE1.md:532). This over-count pushes toward STOP. No doc in the repo mentions it. This comes from reading the code. It was not measured, and on a macOS window the card may fit on screen.
fix: Scope the heading and the summary to the defect: 'the not-yet-loaded-price defect biases toward STOP BUILDING'. Add one line: 'The ledger's net bias is not established. offerAppeared fires on screen appearance, not on the offer card becoming visible (RoadView.swift:40-57), so a counter can show offerAppeared > 0 when the price was never on screen.' Leave the fix for P1-11 to decide.
